resolutions.researcher_notes: Sheet records StartState/Province=Pennsylvania, StartCountryOrArea=United States, EndState/Province=Ohio, EndCountryOrArea=United States. Could NOT corroborate this — the two primary documents on this row that actually state the pipeline's termini both put BOTH endpoints in West Virginia, not PA/OH: (1) Columbia Pipeline Group's own 2015 Leach XPress FAQ (already staged on this row for Diameter/Length) states verbatim under 'What is the proposed pipeline route?': 'The Leach XPress pipeline will originate in Marshall County, West Virginia and travel through southwestern Pennsylvania and southeastern Ohio and end in Wayne County, West Virginia.' (2) The Federal Register FERC notice of application (already staged on this row for Capacity/Fuel/Length/Operator) lists project facilities as 'located in Marshall and Wayne Counties, West Virginia, Greene County, Pennsylvania, and Monroe, Noble, Muskingum, Morgan, Perry Fairfield, Hocking, Jackson, Lawrence and Vinton Counties, Ohio' -- i.e. WV at both ends (Marshall Co. in the north, Wayne Co. in the south), with PA and OH counties in between, matching the FAQ's route description. A third source, Natural Gas Intelligence's 2015 filing story, independently corroborates the southern (Wayne County, WV) terminus: it reports 'an interconnection with Columbia Gulf near Leach, KY' -- Leach, Kentucky sits on the WV/KY line immediately adjacent to Wayne County, WV, consistent with the FAQ's stated end point. I searched all refs already opened on this row plus the FERC docket cover story and found no document stating a PA-to-OH route; every route-specific source found is WV-to-WV via PA/OH. This is not a rounding-tolerance disagreement (a different state at both ends, not a close number), so I have NOT forced it to REFS_ADDED against the recorded value -- flagging as a likely sheet error for the orchestrator/human to review and correct (recommend StartState/Province=West Virginia [Marshall County], EndState/Province=West Virginia [Wayne County], with Pennsylvania/Ohio as transited states, not endpoints).

verifications.note: AGU Landslide Blog (Dave Petley, 23 Jul 2018), opening line: 'Leach XPress is a new $1.75 billion pipeline that transports large volumes of shale gas from the Marcellus and Utica regions of Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio...' -- exact match to recorded SegmentCost=1,750,000,000 USD, and names the pipeline directly.

TransCanada's own 1/2/2018 in-service announcement: 'LXP comprises 160 miles (257 kilometres) of 36-inch-diameter pipeline, three compressor stations, and modifications to an existing compressor station. Representing an investment of approximately US$1.6 billion...' -- names Leach XPress (LXP) specifically (not a combined figure with Mountaineer/Gulf XPress, which are given separately in the same release) and states an approximate cost close to, but ~8.6% below, the recorded $1.75B.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded SegmentCost=1,750,000,000.00 USD. The AGU Landslide Blog states the project cost as 'a new $1.75 billion pipeline' -- an exact match, and independent of the pipeline's own sponsor (it is a landslide-hazard blog by a geoscientist, discussing the June 2018 Leach XPress rupture, that opens by describing the pipeline). TransCanada/TC Energy's own Jan 2018 press release separately states 'approximately US$1.6 billion' as LXP's investment -- same order of magnitude and same pipeline (release explicitly separates LXP's figure from the combined MXP/GXP figures elsewhere in the release), but ~$150M / 8.6% below the recorded $1.75B; noted here as a discrepancy worth a validity check given the gap exceeds simple rounding, but the sponsor's 'approximately' figure and the AGU blog's exact figure are consistent enough (same $1.6-1.75B order) that I read this as REFS_ADDED at high tier rather than UNRESOLVED, carrying the recorded value forward. Did not find a FERC-filed capital-cost estimate or SEC/10-K figure for LXP specifically to adjudicate the sponsor-vs-blog gap further; a targeted cost validity check against TC Energy's 10-K/40-F capex disclosures for FY2016-2018 could resolve which figure is more precise.
